questions.question: Which type of carbohydrate CANNOT be broken down by the Gl tract, does not provide energy, but helps the body get rid of wastes and keeps the intestinal tract healthy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fibre.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Fibre is a type of carbohydrate that the body can't digest.
 
• Though most carbohydrates are broken down into sugar molecules called glucose, fibre cannot be broken down into sugar molecules, and instead, it passes through the body undigested.
 
• Dietary fibre comes from plant-based foods that contain cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, pectin, mucilage, and gum.
 
• Your digestive system lacks the enzymes to break down these food components, and they travel through your gut without being digested.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​Starch is a soft, white, tasteless powder that is insoluble in cold water, alcohol, or other solvents.
 
• The basic chemical formula of the starch molecule is (C6H10O5)n.
 
• Sugar is the generic name for sweet-tasting, soluble carbohydrates, many of which are used in food.
 
• This stored form of glucose is made up of many connected glucose molecules and is called glycogen.

questions.question: What is the mode of adaptation done by aquatic plants and animals where the osmotic concentration of the body fluids changes with that of the ambient air and water osmotic concentration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Conform.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **aquatic organisms** in which the **osmotic concentration** and **temperature of the body** change according to the ambient conditions of water are referred to as **conformers**.
 
• The natural source of water that is present in our surroundings in the environment like in ponds, lakes, rivers etc. is termed as ambient water.
 
• The osmotic concentration of that water is '**ambient water osmotic concentration**'.
 
• **Osmoregulation** is the active regulation of the osmotic pressure of an organism 's fluids to maintain the **homeostasis** of the organism 's water content.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Migrate** - to move from one country or region to another Families migrated west in search of work. 
 
• **Suspend** - The state in which the particles of a substance are dispersed but not totally dissolved in a fluid.
 
• Biological regulation is what allows an organism to handle the effects of a perturbation, modulating its own constitutive dynamics in response to particular changes in internal and external conditions.

questions.question: Which river basin covers an area of 65,145 km², of which about 80% liesin Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Tapi Basin.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Tapi Basin is situated in the northern part of the Deccan Plateau and extends over an area of 65145 sqkm which is nearly 2% of the total geographical area of the country.
 
• Nearly 80% of the basin lies in the State of Maharashtra.
 
• It lies between 72°33’ to 78°17’ east longitudes and 20°9’ to 21°50’ north latitudes. 
 
• The basin is bounded by the Satpura range on the north, by the Mahadev hills on the east, by the Ajanta Range and the Satmala hills on the south and by the Arabian Sea on the west.
 
• The Tapi is the second largest westward draining river of the Peninsula.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Godavari basin**. The Godavari River basin is the longest river in Maharashtra and the second-longest river in India after Ganga. 
 
• The total length of the river is 1,465 km.
 
• Godavari river rises near Nasik in Maharashtra at an elevation of about 1067 m and flows for a length of about **1465 km** before outfalling into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• 
 
 
 **The Godavari** originates in the Western Ghats of central India near Nashik in Maharashtra, from the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: In 1869, who named a new term 'Oecologie' that defined the study of the relationship of organisms with their environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ernst Haeckel.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1869, Ernst Haeckel named a new term 'Oecologie' that defined the study of the relationship of organisms with their environment.
 
• Ecology was originally defined in the mid-19th century when biology was a vastly different discipline than it is today.
 
• The original definition is from **Ernst Haeckel**, who defined ecology as the study of the relationship of organisms with their environment.
 
• The term ecology is believed to have been coined by **Ernst Haeckel** in 1869 though its first authentic use was made by Reiter in 1885.
 
• It is used to describe the “economies” of living forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the first ecologists whose writings survive may have been **Aristotle or perhaps his student, Theophrastus**, both of whom had an interest in many species of animals and plants.
 
• Theophrastus described interrelationships between animals and their environment as early as the 4th century BC.
 
• '**Ramdeo Misra**' is known as the father of Ecology in India.

• Some significant trees of a montane temperate forest are **rhododendrons, ferns, oak, maple, juniper, deodar, chilgoza**, etc.
 
• These types of forests are found in the state of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are mainly two types of tropical forests that are found in the Himalayas - the **tropical rainforests, and the tropical deciduous forests**.
 
• The tropical rainforests are dense, evergreen, gloomy, and, similar to the forests of the Amazon basin and other equatorial areas.
 
• **Oak, laurel, and, chestnut trees** are also found up to 7,000 feet above sea level.
 
• Pine trees are found up to 12,000 feet above sea level; above that point only lichens, grass, and moss can be found since it is so cold in the higher regions.

questions.question: Which group of animals has a body wall composed of both circular and longitudinal muscle fibres surrounded by a moist, cellular cuticle that is secreted by an epidermal epithelium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Annelida.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Besides being segmented, the body wall of Annelida is characterized by being made up of both circular and longitudinal muscle fibres surrounded by a moist, acellular cuticle that is secreted by an epidermal epithelium.
 
• The body cavity of annelids is lined by epithelium.
 
• Successive body segments are separated by walls that correspond to the external rings. 
 
• In grooves between the segments of some oligochaetes are dorsal pores through which coelomic fluid may be discharged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phylum Arthropoda **contains a wide diversity of animals with hard exoskeletons and jointed appendages.**
 
• The flatworms, flatworms, Platyhelminthes, or platyhelminths are a phylum of relatively simple bilaterian, unsegmented, soft-bodied invertebrates.
 
• Coelenterata is **a term encompassing the animal phyla Cnidaria (coral animals, true jellies, sea anemones, sea pens, and their relatives) and Ctenophora (comb jellies)**.
